title: Weights of the cohomology of a finite boundary
statement:
Let $Z_0$ be finite over $k_0$ and let $\mathcal G$ be a
constructible Weil sheaf whose stalks have weights at most $w$. Then
$H_c^0(Z,\mathcal G)$ has weights at most $w$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-finite-weil-sections-decomposition] to $Z_0$ and $\mathcal G$. Thus $V=H_c^0(Z,\mathcal G)$ is a finite-dimensional Frobenius module, and the evaluation maps $e_z:V\to\mathcal G_z$, indexed by the finitely many geometric points over the closed points $x$, jointly detect zero. For $d_x=[\kappa(x):k_0]\geq1$, the precise compatibility is $e_zF^{d_x}=F_{x,z}e_z$. In particular it is the local return operator $F_{x,z}$, not the global $q$-Frobenius itself, which acts on an individual stalk.

source.place: Opening evaluation assertion and displayed formula, corrected using Stacks Tag 03QP

proof.text: For a closed point $x$ and a geometric lift $z$, interpret the stalk-weight hypothesis in the local normalization $q_x=q^{d_x}$ of [def-weil-punctual-weights]. If it is expressed as a mixed filtration, use [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights] with base $q_x$: its finite stable filtration has pure graded pieces of weights $u\leq w$. By [p-linear-filtration] the characteristic polynomial of $F_{x,z}$ is the product of those of the graded pieces. A root of that product is a root of one factor, so every eigenvalue $\alpha$ of $F_{x,z}$ has $|\iota(\alpha)|=q_x^{u/2}\leq q_x^{w/2}$, since $q_x>1$. If the hypothesis is already given as the punctual eigenvalue bound, this is exactly that bound. This also treats zero stalks, whose characteristic polynomial has no roots.

source.place: The assertion that the stalk-weight hypothesis bounds every local eigenvalue; the filtration-to-spectrum implication is made explicit

proof.text: Let $\lambda$ be an eigenvalue of $F$ and choose $v\ne0$ with $Fv=\lambda v$. Some component $e_z(v)$ is nonzero; let $x$ be its underlying closed point and $d=d_x$. Iterating $Fv=\lambda v$ gives $F^dv=\lambda^dv$, so the return identity of [lem-a1-finite-weil-sections-decomposition] gives $F_{x,z}e_z(v)=\lambda^de_z(v)$. Therefore $\lambda^d$ is an eigenvalue of the local stalk operator. The local eigenvalue bound established in step 2 gives $|\iota(\lambda^d)|\leq(q^d)^{w/2}$. Since $\iota$ is a field isomorphism, $|\iota(\lambda)|^d\leq(q^{w/2})^d$. Both bases are nonnegative and $d\geq1$, so taking the increasing $d$-th root yields $|\iota(\lambda)|\leq q^{w/2}$. This proves the required spectral bound without any diagonalization or assertion about arithmetic invariant subspaces.

source.place: Final weight argument, with the missing degree normalization and the nonzero eigenvector-component calculation supplied

proof.text: Every eigenvalue of the finite-dimensional Frobenius module $(V,F)$ satisfies the bound just proved. Apply [lem-a1-punctual-bound-module-mixed] to obtain that $(V,F)$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$, as required. If $V=0$, there are no eigenvalues and the same cited lemma applies; equivalently its mixed filtration is the empty one.

source.place: Last sentence, passage from eigenvalue bounds to the Frobenius-module weight bound

proof_origin.place: Corrected proof: geometric stalk evaluation, degree-d local return operators, and an eigenvector argument

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q24-081d71fab (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no changes. I read the item, the new child, every cited statement, the unit sk-thm-dl-a1-upper, and Stacks 03QP (etale-cohomology.tex lines 8245-8264). The blueprint's display H_c^0 = sum of Gal-invariants of the stalks is false. Counterexamples: over Spec F_q with Frobenius -1 the invariants are 0 but the stalk has dimension 1; over Spec F_{q^2} with the constant sheaf the formula gives dimension 1 instead of 2. The repair keeps the blueprint's evaluate-then-bound route. Step 1 takes exactly what the child states. Step 2 is elementary: with local base q_x=q^{d_x}, p-linear-filtration bounds every local eigenvalue. Step 3 is elementary: a nonzero component e_z(v) of an eigenvector gives lambda^d as a local eigenvalue, and the d-th root gives |iota lambda|<=q^{w/2}. This normalization was missing in the old proof. Step 4 applies lem-a1-punctual-bound-module-mixed, whose hypotheses steps 1 and 3 supply. The child is true by 03QP(1) at the geometric point of Spec k. P_x matches the d_x embeddings of kappa(x), and Frobenius returns as in def-weil-local-frobenius-trace. I tested it on empty Z_0, degree 1 and 2 points, a nonreduced point and a Jordan block. It carries no weights, so it is not a restated clause of the parent, and no DAG node states it (the lem-trf-* and pbc candidates are finite-coefficient or ordinary sheaves). It meets B1-B9 with three kinds of search, and its coefficients are the same common-stage Qlb as the item's. The citers supply the hypothesis as the punctual eigenvalue bound, which matches step 2. Batch-5 check: all five flagged citations are general definitions, not steps in the proofs of the trace formula or Poincare duality. They are the Frobenius module and its weights (sk-def-frobmod), the constructible heart, H_c, global F and local F_y. The heart and F_y were already reached through def-weil-punctual-weights before this delivery. The item uses neither assumption. lean.statement: theorem sf_finiteBoundary_hasWeightsAtMost (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p) (Qbar : Type v) [Field Qbar] [Algebra (Padic l) Qbar] [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Qbar] (iota : Qbar ≃+* ℂ) (Z₀ : Over (Spec (.of D.k₀))) [IsFinite Z₀.hom] (G : sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl Z₀ Qbar) (w : ℝ) (hG : ∀ (y : {y : Z₀.left // y ∈ closedPoints Z₀.left}) (α : Qbar), SfPunctualEigenvalue D l hl Qbar Z₀ G y α → ‖iota α‖ ≤ (Nat.card (Z₀.left.residueField y.val) : ℝ) ^ (w / 2)) : SfIsMixedOfWeightsAtMost D l hl Qbar (sfWeilCohomologyPoint D) iota (commonStageCompactWeilCohomology D l hl Qbar Z₀ (Compactification.ofIsProper Z₀.hom) G 0) w
lean.note: Uses the recorded common-stage Weil heart and local punctual eigenvalues, not the older upstream WeilSheaf. H_c^0 with Frobenius is retained as the canonical compact-support higher image on Spec(k₀); punctual mixedness there is exactly Frobenius-module mixedness under the geometric coefficient-fibre equivalence. The original source statement is unchanged. The newly cited landed definition supplies that canonical higher image; the ordinary/compact cohomology dependency is repaired in this packet to expose its common-stage specialization.
